name: MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher
title: WorkspaceSwitcher
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (ghost) with MonarchAvatar and androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuDefaults.TrailingIcon; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem for up to five workspaces, otherwise androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with MonarchSearchBar and an androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn of selectable rows with androidx.compose.material3.RadioButton
summary: Switches between the workspaces a person belongs to from a button with the workspace's logo, name and handle, which opens a menu for a short list or a searchable sheet for a long one, with Create workspace and All workspaces.
whenToUse: At the top of a product's navigation drawer or top bar, when a person can belong to several workspaces.
whenNotToUse: To filter the app to a part of one workspace, use MonarchSpaceSwitcher. For a searchable choice inside a form, use MonarchCombobox.
api: @Composable fun MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher(workspaces: List<MonarchWorkspaceOption>, selection: String?, onSelectionChange: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, iconOnly: Boolean = false, onCreate: (() -> Unit)? = null, onManage: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels = MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels())
class MonarchWorkspaceOption(id: String, name: String, handle: String? = null, logo: Painter? = null, keywords: String? = null)

class MonarchWorkspaceSwitcherLabels(label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, search: String? = null, empty: String? = null, loading: String? = null, create: String? = null, manage: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: workspaces
options.description: The workspaces this person belongs to, in display order.

options.name: selection
options.description: The current workspace id, null when none is chosen.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Called with the chosen workspace id; the app switches. Choosing the current one again does not call it.

options.name: size
options.description: The height and padding of the button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu or sheet can be opened.

options.name: loading
options.description: The workspaces are still loading: the button opens the sheet, which says Loading workspaces….

options.name: iconOnly
options.description: Shows only the logo and the arrow. TalkBack still reads the name and handle.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Adds Create workspace, which closes the menu or sheet and runs this.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds All workspaces, which closes the menu or sheet and runs this.

states.name: menu
states.description: Up to five loaded workspaces: a Material 3 dropdown menu with logos, names and handles, the current one with a radio mark, then a divider and the actions.

states.name: sheet
states.description: More than five workspaces, or loading: a modal bottom sheet with a search field and a list of single-choice rows.

states.name: nothing chosen
states.description: The button shows the initial of Workspace and Choose a workspace.

states.name: searching
states.description: The sheet keeps workspaces whose name, handle or keywords contain the text, ignoring case and accents; with no match it reads No workspaces match.

states.name: loading
states.description: The sheet ends with Loading workspaces….

states.name: disabled
states.description: The ghost button's disabled colors; the menu or sheet cannot open.

appearance: A ghost button with a square MonarchAvatar logo, the name in label text with the handle in muted caption text and the Material exposed-dropdown arrow. The menu and sheet use the raised surface and Material radio marks. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map lists combobox as a dependency; MonarchCombobox is a labelled form field without logos, so the switcher has its own button and reuses the sheet of MonarchSpaceSwitcher. As on iOS, the presentation is chosen by count: a Material 3 DropdownMenu for up to five workspaces (unlike the iOS menu it can show logos and handles) and a searchable sheet beyond that, replacing the web's popover listbox. The web's tooltip on the collapsed trigger is the spoken value. manageHref and createHref are callbacks (onManage, onCreate): components do not navigate. The web's controlled open state and align are not offered. Logos are Painters loaded by the app. iOS uses a Binding, isIconOnly and manageURL; Android hoists selection with onSelectionChange, drops the is prefix and takes onManage. Experimental: an identity product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The button is one element named "Workspace" whose state description is the name and handle ("Acme, @acme"), built by a tested pure function, also when only the logo shows; it keeps a 48dp touch target.
Menu items are read as the name and handle and the current one has the selected state and a radio mark.
Sheet rows are radio-button elements read as the name and handle; the chosen row is selected.
Logos are decorative; messages in the sheet are polite live regions; Cancel and the back gesture close without a change.
Menu items, rows and actions are at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: Choosing the current workspace again closes without calling onSelectionChange.
A selection that is not in workspaces reads as Choose a workspace.
Keywords are matched by search but never shown.
The search text is cleared when the sheet closes.

var workspace by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>({{value}}) }
val uriHandler = LocalUriHandler.current
examples.setup:
var workspace by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>("w1") }
val uriHandler = LocalUriHandler.current

examples.title: Many workspaces open a searchable sheet
examples.setup:
var workspace by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>("w1") }
val workspaces = (1..8).map { MonarchWorkspaceOption("w$it", "Client $it", handle = "client$it") }
examples.code:
MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher(
    workspaces = workspaces,
    selection = workspace,
    onSelectionChange = { workspace = it },
    size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web names this control with one sentence ("Workspace: Acme @acme"). On Android TalkBack gets the control name and its current value as the control's name and state description ("Workspace", "Acme, @acme"), which it speaks as one phrase and announces again when the value changes; the same words are visible in the control.
parityExceptions.convention: a control has a name and a state, not a joined sentence (Android accessibility: contentDescription + stateDescription)
